The core of the offensive strategy lies in a fixed 8-play architecture, where each play is defined by a specific distribution of slants and runs. This combinatorial structure ensures deterministic behavior under idealized conditions. The principle of line advancement introduces a dynamic constraint: if resistance exceeds line force, the line must yield. This creates a binary outcome—either advance or retreat—based on force equilibrium. Backs must initiate immediately to maintain momentum, violating this constraint leads to loss of kinetic energy. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each element's failure propagates through the entire sequence. The system exhibits strong duality between spatial distribution (route types) and temporal execution (timing of actions), with failure modes tied to both structural rigidity and dynamic timing violations.
